analysis.title: GS Crook - 2 Mins: Volatile Week Ahead Risk Thoughts 22 Nov 2026
key_insights: Tech-heavy indices are oversold (NDX, SOX, Info Tech GICS) with valuations at over 10-year lows (NDX ~17x fwd P/E, semis ~12-13x). Conditions for a bounce are present but year-end rally optimism has faded.

Fundamentals look firm (big beat/raise from KEYS, NVDA, PANW) yet price action shows a buyers strike with rotational unwind under the hood. Estimate revisions likely move higher with DELL, MU, AVGO, HPE earnings ahead, so charts and companies disagree.

The 2018 analog (NDX 4Q18) has gone mainstream. GS Baskets suggests High Beta Cyclicals (GSXUHBCY) as a short if growth downgrades ensue, and the Conditional Downvar Strategy (GSISCVS1) as deep OTM protection, 2.5% above barrier.

Baskets prefers Healthcare over Staples, wants to avoid value traps like China Competition, and warns on crowded positions. Beta-adjusted nets are at 5-year lows but real money positioning is not low.

Positioning is washed out per GS Equity Sales: prime book net exposure at multi-year lows, global positioning near 10-year lows, HFs sold tech at the fastest pace on record over 6 weeks, CTAs near the bottom of the 10-year range in NDX futures. CFTC non-dealer positioning is still near highs. They see this as closer to the end than the beginning.

Equity vol is in extreme stress: SPX down seven straight sessions, VIX near 30, term structure aggressively inverted, skew very steep. GS US vol panic index is 9.2 of 10, and readings above 9.5 historically signal near-term relief.

Portfolio Strategy sees three bottom conditions: AI news improving earnings confidence, a better macro backdrop (lower oil, dovish Fed), or a major positioning decline. It sees AI infrastructure best returns behind us and recommends owning hyperscalers instead.

Hyperscaler cloud revenue growth accelerated from 25% in 2024 to 54% in Q3 2026, with revenue backlogs totaling $1.8 trillion. Slowing capex growth is positive for hyperscaler free cash flow if demand is not the cause.

Macro has been hostile: adversarial Fed, Waller calling for 50bp in December, hot jobs report and hot CPI, tighter FCIs. Upcoming catalysts are core PCE, NFP, the December Fed, and November CPI in mid-December. Privorotsky is ready to be contrarian and notes vol is hard to sustain into the US holiday week.

Snider says the key question is where earnings come from after the AI capex build-out. Q3 S&P 500 earnings growth was over 35%, so the issue is forward looking. Lower oil and rates or continued AI advancement could provide the new source.

Wilson cites cracks in the AI story (financing needs, peaking investment impulse, forward earnings worries), credit pressure, a fresh Fed tightening cycle and political shifts. There is no single macro worry and no clear floor, but the bounce prospects in coming weeks are clearly better.

GIR semis sees stocks pricing in peak concerns with a more favorable medium-term risk/reward. Catalysts over six months include hyperscaler 2027 capex budgets, 2028 datacenter visibility, and hyperscaler/frontier lab funding health.

GIR memory/storage: prefers Buy SNDK over Neutral MU as NAND supply constraints may outlast DRAM. Prefers Buy STX over Neutral WDC, as Toshiba's capacity add worsened sentiment but likely has limited pricing impact.
GIR analog: Buy SITM (50%+ AI datacenter exposure, precision timing), plus Buy MCHP, ADI, NXPI on end-market exposure and idiosyncratic drivers.
